claim: Rab10 is critical for TrkB sorting and propagation of BDNF signalling from axon terminals to the soma.
source: In this work, we use primary mouse neurons to uncover the small GTPase Rab10 as critical for TrkB sorting and propagation of BDNF signalling from axon terminals to the soma.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by multiple experimental results throughout the manuscript.

claim: Rab10 defines a novel membrane compartment that is rapidly mobilised towards the axon terminal upon BDNF stimulation.
source: Our data demonstrate that Rab10 defines a novel membrane compartment that is rapidly mobilised towards the axon terminal upon BDNF stimulation, enabling the axon to fine-tune retrograde signalling depending on BDNF availability at the synapse.
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell imaging data showing directional changes in Rab10 organelle transport upon BDNF stimulation.

claim: Rab10 polymorphisms are associated with a neuroprotective phenotype in Alzheimer's disease.
source: These results help clarifying the neuroprotective phenotype recently associated to Rab10 polymorphisms in Alzheimer's disease and provide a new therapeutic target to halt neurodegeneration.
evidence: This claim references recent findings about Rab10 polymorphisms in Alzheimer's disease without providing direct experimental evidence in this manuscript.

claim: Neurotrophic factors secreted by target tissues regulate local cytoskeletal dynamics to promote or cease axon elongation, induce branching, and synaptic maturation and plasticity.
source: A clear example is provided by neurotrophic factors secreted by target tissues and sensed by axon terminals, where, among other functions, they regulate local cytoskeletal dynamics to promote or cease axon elongation, induce branching, as well as synaptic maturation and plasticity (Andres-Alonso et al., 2019; Szobota et al., 2019; Woo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activated receptors are internalised and targeted to the retrograde axonal transport pathway within signalling endosomes.
source: At the same time, a population of activated receptors are internalised and targeted to the retrograde axonal transport pathway within signalling endosomes (Barford et al., 2017; Villarroel-Campos et al., 2018), which propagate neurotrophic signalling towards the cell body, regulating gene expression, dendritic branching, and the balance between survival and apoptosis (Du and Poo, 2004; Pazyra-Murphy et al., 2009; Watson et al., 1999; Zhou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: BDNF and TrkB play a critical role in the formation, maintenance, and plasticity of neuronal circuits.
source: By activating diverse signalling cascades, comprising the phosphoinositide 3‐kinase (PI3K)‐Akt pathway, mitogen‐activated protein kinases (MAPKs), and phospholipase C‐gamma (PLCγ), BDNF and TrkB play a critical role in the formation, maintenance, and plasticity of neuronal circuits (Huang and Reichardt, 2003; Minichiello, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Binding of BDNF at synaptic sites leads to endocytosis of TrkB and entry of the activated ligand–receptor complexes in early endosomes.
source: Binding of BDNF at synaptic sites leads to endocytosis of TrkB and entry of the activated ligand–receptor complexes in early endosomes (Deinhardt et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A pool of internalised TrkB receptors is sorted to signalling endosomes and engage with the cytoplasmic dynein motor complex for transport to the soma.
source: Whilst part of internalised TrkB recycle back to the plasma membrane, a pool of receptors is sorted to signalling endosomes and engage with the cytoplasmic dynein motor complex, which mediates the transport of these organelles to the soma (Andres-Alonso et al., 2019; Ha et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Signalling endosomes are generated from early endosomes that mature into a more specialised organelle escaping acidification and lysosomal degradation.
source: Independent lines of evidence indicate that this compartment is generated from early endosomes that then mature into a more specialised organelle escaping acidification and lysosomal degradation (Villarroel-Campos et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Early endosome formation is regulated by Rab5.
source: Whilst early endosome formation is regulated by Rab5, maturation and processive transport of signalling endosomes in different neuronal models are controlled by Rab7 (Bucci et al., 2014; Burk et al., 2017; Deinhardt et al., 2006; Kucharava et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Maturation and processive transport of signalling endosomes are controlled by Rab7.
source: Whilst early endosome formation is regulated by Rab5, maturation and processive transport of signalling endosomes in different neuronal models are controlled by Rab7 (Bucci et al., 2014; Burk et al., 2017; Deinhardt et al., 2006; Kucharava et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10-positive organelles are transported both anterogradely and retrogradely along axons in hippocampal neurons.
source: In this work, we specifically focused on Rab10 since it has been shown that Rab10-positive organelles are transported both anterogradely and retrogradely along axons in hippocampal neurons (Deng et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 was significantly enriched in neurotrophin signalling endosomes isolated from mouse embryonic stem cell‐derived motor neurons.
source: Previous work from our laboratory using an affinity purification approach to isolate neurotrophin signalling endosomes from mouse embryonic stem cell‐derived motor neurons found that Rab10 was significantly enriched in this axonal compartment, which is also characterised by the presence of Rab5 and Rab7 (Debaisieux et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work from the authors' laboratory.

claim: 48 hours of doxycycline treatment with shRNA Rab10 consistently halved the number of neurons per field compared to control.
source: We observed that 48 hr of treatment consistently halved the number of cells per field compared to control group, whereas incubation for 24 hr did not affect neuronal density (Figure 1a and b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a and b.

claim: 24 hours of doxycycline treatment with shRNA Rab10 did not affect neuronal density.
source: We observed that 48 hr of treatment consistently halved the number of cells per field compared to control group, whereas incubation for 24 hr did not affect neuronal density (Figure 1a and b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a and b.

claim: Rab10 immunoreactivity significantly decreased at both 24 and 48 hours after addition of doxycycline compared to control lentivirus.
source: Rab10 immunoreactivity appeared significantly decreased at both 24 and 48 hr after addition of doxycycline compared to control lentivirus (Figure 1a and c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a and c.

claim: TrkB expression levels were comparable at 48 hours of treatment with shRNA Rab10.
source: We observed comparable levels of TrkB even at 48 hr of treatment with shRNA Rab10 (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Axonal TrkB can be detected in the cell body of neurons stimulated with BDNF after 2.5 hours.
source: After 2.5 hr, we were able to detect axonal TrkB in the cell body of neurons stimulated with BDNF, but not in neurons depleted of BDNF by addition of an anti-BDNF-blocking antibody (Figure 2b), confirming the specificity of the antibody and the overall reliability of our retrograde accumulation assay.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Neurons treated with shRNA targeting Rab10 showed decreased retrograde accumulation of TrkB compared to control transduced neurons.
source: Neurons transduced with the shRNA Rab10 and treated with doxycycline for 18–22 hr showed lower levels of endogenous Rab10 (Figure 2c, grey) and significantly reduced retrograde accumulation of TrkB compared with neurons expressing control lentivirus (Figure 2c and d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c and d.

claim: There is a significant correlation between Rab10 expression and TrkB accumulation in neurons.
source: Moreover, when we take both populations together, we found a significant correlation between Rab10 expression and TrkB accumulation, strongly suggesting that Rab10 plays a role in retrograde axonal transport of internalised TrkB (Figure 2e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Neurons treated with shRNA directed against Rab10 showed a significant decrease in nuclear pCREB after axonal BDNF stimulation.
source: Neurons treated with an shRNA directed against Rab10 showed a significant decrease in nuclear pCREB (Figure 2f and g), which was rescued by treatment of Rab10 knockdown cells with a lentivirus encoding shRNA-resistant Rab10, further confirming the specificity of this effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f and g.

claim: The decrease in nuclear pCREB upon Rab10 knockdown was rescued by expression of shRNA-resistant Rab10.
source: Neurons treated with an shRNA directed against Rab10 showed a significant decrease in nuclear pCREB (Figure 2f and g), which was rescued by treatment of Rab10 knockdown cells with a lentivirus encoding shRNA-resistant Rab10, further confirming the specificity of this effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f and g.

claim: Most signalling endosomes are positive for Rab7.
source: Most of these axonal carriers are positive for Rab7 (Deinhardt et al., 2006), which enables the recruitment of the dynein motor complex and their processive retrograde transport along microtubules (Ha et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab7 enables the recruitment of the dynein motor complex and processive retrograde transport of signalling endosomes along microtubules.
source: Most of these axonal carriers are positive for Rab7 (Deinhardt et al., 2006), which enables the recruitment of the dynein motor complex and their processive retrograde transport along microtubules (Ha et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 and Rab7 show a very low degree of overlap in neurons stimulated with BDNF.
source: We found that Rab10 (orange) and Rab7 (green) consistently showed a very low degree of overlap (see yellow regions in Figure 3a and superposition of intensity peaks in Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 3a and b.

claim: Rab10 and Rab5 partially co-localise in a population of organelles.
source: On the other hand, the super-resolution imaging revealed a population of organelles where Rab10 (orange) and Rab5 (purple) partially co-localise (see pink regions, Figure 3a), suggesting that Rab5-positive retrograde carriers (Goto-Silva et al., 2019), or stationary early endosomes, could also contain Rab10.
evidence: This claim is supported by super-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Rab10 and Rab5 have around 20% co-localisation with a significant increase in the amount of Rab5 in Rab10 domains when stimulated with BDNF.
source: Rab10 and Rab5 were confirmed to have around 20% co-localisation and a significant increase in the amount of Rab5 in Rab10 domains when stimulated with BDNF (Figure 3c).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data and co-localisation analysis shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Rab10 and Rab7 exhibit very low co-localisation levels, which is unaffected by BDNF stimulation.
source: On the other hand, Rab10 and Rab7 were found to exhibit very low co-localisation levels, which was unaffected by BDNF stimulation, suggesting that Rab10 is more likely to be associated with early components of the endosomal system rather than mature and processive signalling endosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data and co-localisation analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The proportion of TrkB present in Rab10 compartments is very low and remains constant across 30, 60, and 90 minutes post-endocytosis.
source: However, the proportion of TrkB present in Rab10 compartments is very low and remains constant across the duration of the experiment (white).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e and f.

claim: TrkB localises transiently on Rab10-positive membrane compartments en route to its delivery to axonal retrograde carriers.
source: These results provide another evidence suggesting that TrkB localises transiently on Rab10-positive membrane compartments en route to its delivery to axonal retrograde carriers.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing low and constant triple co-localisation of TrkB/HCT/Rab10.

claim: Approximately 60% of retrograde TrkB carriers are positive for Rab10 when EGFP-Rab10 is overexpressed.
source: Quantification of five independent experiments confirmed that approximately 60% of retrograde TrkB carriers are positive for Rab10 under these experimental conditions (Figure 4d).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: No anterograde TrkB/Rab10 double-positive compartments were observed.
source: Interestingly, no anterograde TrkB/Rab10 double-positive compartments were observed, suggesting that TrkB is present in organelles with a strong retrograde bias.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: 29.6% of anterograde p75NTR-containing organelles were found positive for Rab10.
source: On average, 29.6% of anterograde and 15.5% of retrograde p75NTR-containing organelles were found positive for Rab10 across five independent experiments (Figure 4h).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 4h.

claim: 15.5% of retrograde p75NTR-containing organelles were found positive for Rab10.
source: On average, 29.6% of anterograde and 15.5% of retrograde p75NTR-containing organelles were found positive for Rab10 across five independent experiments (Figure 4h).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 4h.

claim: BDNF-depleted axons exhibit a bias towards retrograde Rab10 transport.
source: Quantification of five independent experiments shows that BDNF-depleted axons exhibit a bias towards retrograde Rab10 transport, which significantly switches to anterograde after 10 min of stimulation with BDNF (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Rab10 transport significantly switches to anterograde after 10 minutes of stimulation with BDNF.
source: Quantification of five independent experiments shows that BDNF-depleted axons exhibit a bias towards retrograde Rab10 transport, which significantly switches to anterograde after 10 min of stimulation with BDNF (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The axonal pool of KIF13B appears to decrease after stimulation with BDNF.
source: Interestingly, the axonal pool of KIF13B appears to decrease after stimulation with BDNF, whereas that of KIF5B increases under the same experimental conditions, suggesting that the total axonal content of these kinesins may be differentially regulated by BDNF signalling.
evidence: This claim is supported by high-resolution confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6a and d.

claim: The axonal pool of KIF5B increases after stimulation with BDNF.
source: Interestingly, the axonal pool of KIF13B appears to decrease after stimulation with BDNF, whereas that of KIF5B increases under the same experimental conditions, suggesting that the total axonal content of these kinesins may be differentially regulated by BDNF signalling.
evidence: This claim is supported by high-resolution confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6a and d.

claim: There is a statistically significant 12.7% increase in the amount of KIF13B recruited to Rab10-positive organelles upon BDNF stimulation.
source: Quantification of the intensity of KIF13B in Rab10-positive areas (Figure 6b) reveals a statistically significant 12.7% increase in the amount of the motor recruited to Rab10-positive organelles.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The ratio between the Rab10-positive and total KIF13B-positive area in the axon remained unchanged at 7.3% after BDNF stimulation.
source: On the other hand, Figure 6c shows that the ratio between the Rab10-positive and total KIF13B-positive area in the axon remained unchanged (7.3% of the area), suggesting that the proportion of double KIF13B/Rab10 compartments remains constant.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: There is no significant change in the KIF5B intensity ratio in Rab10-positive domains after BDNF stimulation.
source: In contrast, when we performed the same analysis for KIF5B, we found that, despite its overall increase in the axon upon BDNF stimulation, there is no significant change in the intensity ratio in Rab10-positive domains (Figure 6e).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: The proportion of KIF5B axonal organelles that overlap with Rab10 is around 4% and remained unchanged after BDNF stimulation.
source: Consistently, Figure 6f shows that the proportion of KIF5B axonal organelles that overlap with Rab10 is lower than KIF13B (around 4% of the area) and remained unchanged after BDNF stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: There is an average twofold increase in the KIF13B/Rab10 ratio when N2A cells were stimulated with BDNF.
source: Quantification of three independent experiments (Figure 6h) show an average twofold increase in the KIF13B/Rab10 ratio when cells were stimulated with BDNF.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: Rab10 has been shown to regulate multiple processes, including trafficking across early endosomes, the formation of specialised tubular endosomes, the recycling of cargoes back to the plasma membrane, and the targeting of plasmalemmal precursor vesicles.
source: Rab10, on the other hand, has been shown to regulate multiple processes, including trafficking across early endosomes, the formation of specialised tubular endosomes, the recycling of cargoes back to the plasma membrane, as well as the targeting of plasmalemmal precursor vesicles (PPVs), among other functions (Babbey et al., 2006; Brewer et al., 2016; Deng et al., 2014; Etoh and Fukuda, 2019; Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10DN expression does not significantly affect recycling of TrkB compared to EGFP control.
source: Comparison between recycling ratio (recycled/internalised) of EGFP- and Rab10DN-expressing neurons shows no significant differences (Figure 7c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Rab10DN caused a statistically significant increase of internalised TrkB in Rab5-positive domains from 13.2% ± 1.7 to 22.2% ± 2.8.
source: Rab10DN caused a statistically significant increase of internalised TrkB in Rab5-positive domains from 13.2% ± 1.7 to 22.2% ± 2.8, and an increase in the reliability of the co-localisation measurements (CDA p<0.05) (Figure 7e).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-localisation analysis shown in Figure 7e.

claim: Rab10 activity modulates the sorting of activated TrkB receptors from axonal early endosomes to retrograde transport organelles.
source: These results indicate that the probability of finding axonal TrkB in Rab5-positive early endosomes increases in neurons expressing Rab10DN, thus indicating that Rab10 activity modulates the sorting of activated TrkB receptors from axonal early endosomes to retrograde transport organelles.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing increased TrkB retention in Rab5-positive compartments upon Rab10DN expression.

claim: CREB is a transcription factor supporting neuronal survival and differentiation, which is activated by phosphorylation downstream Akt and MAPK signalling.
source: CREB is a transcription factor supporting neuronal survival and differentiation, which is activated by phosphorylation downstream Akt and MAPK signalling (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CREB is required for BDNF-induced dendritic branching.
source: Some of the better characterised early response genes to neurotrophic factors (e.g., Egr1, Egr2, Arc, and cFos) are transcriptional targets of CREB, which is also required for BDNF-induced dendritic branching (Esvald et al., 2020; González-Gutiérrez et al., 2020; Kwon et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Long-distance activation of CREB has been reported from distal axons and dendrites.
source: Long-distance activation of CREB has been reported from distal axons and dendrites, and the endosomal trafficking of phosphorylated TrkB and signalling interactors has been shown to play a crucial role in propagating neurotrophin signalling from the periphery to the nuclear pCREB (Cohen et al., 2011; Riccio et al., 1997; Watson et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 downregulation for 48 hours led to a significant decrease in neuronal density.
source: In our study, we found that Rab10 expression was critical for maintenance and survival of differentiated neurons since its downregulation for 48 hr led to a significant decrease in neuronal density (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Overexpression of dominant-negative mutants of Rab5 leads to decreased neuronal density.
source: Similar effects have been reported upon overexpression of dominant-negative mutants of Rab5, the GTPase mediating the formation of early endosomes, but not for Rab11, which controls the recycling of receptors to the plasma membrane (Lazo et al., 2013; Moya-Alvarado et al., 2018), suggesting that these distinct arms of the endosomal network differentially impact on neuronal homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Overexpression of dominant-negative mutants of Rab11 does not lead to decreased neuronal density.
source: Similar effects have been reported upon overexpression of dominant-negative mutants of Rab5, the GTPase mediating the formation of early endosomes, but not for Rab11, which controls the recycling of receptors to the plasma membrane (Lazo et al., 2013; Moya-Alvarado et al., 2018), suggesting that these distinct arms of the endosomal network differentially impact on neuronal homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 is one of the few Rab GTPases associated with multiple trafficking pathways.
source: Rab10 is one of the few exceptions to this rule, and during the last 30 years, it has been associated to multiple trafficking pathways, including polarised exocytosis from early endosomes, exocytosis in adipocytes and neurons, endoplasmic reticulum dynamics, and the formation of tubular endosomes, to cite but a few (Chua and Tang, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The balance between anterograde and retrograde transport of Rab10-positive organelles is regulated by BDNF.
source: Here we have confirmed previous findings showing that Rab10-positives organelles are present in axons of hippocampal neurons and undergo bidirectional transport (Deng et al., 2014). Importantly, in this work we have demonstrated that the balance between anterograde and retrograde transport of Rab10-positive organelles is regulated by BDNF, indicating the ability of Rab10 to specifically respond to extracellular cues in a signalling context.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from time-lapse microscopy experiments.

claim: A similar function of Rab10 balancing anterograde and retrograde transport has been shown to be required for correct dendritic patterning in Drosophila.
source: A similar function of Rab10 balancing anterograde and retrograde transport has been shown to be required for correct dendritic patterning in Drosophila (Taylor et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: KIF13B and KIF5B are kinesins that distribute preferentially to axons.
source: Given that many kinesins distribute preferentially to distinct neuronal compartments (Hirokawa and Tanaka, 2015), we focused on two kinesins that have been found to be predominant in axons, KIF5B and KIF13B (Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: There is a direct interaction between Rab10 and KIF13A and B, via a Rab-binding domain (RBD)-homology domain.
source: We found that KIF13B, but not KIF5B, increased its relative abundance in axonal Rab10-positive domains (Figure 6a–f), which is in line with the recent evidence indicating a direct interaction between Rab10 and KIF13A and B, via a Rab-binding domain (RBD)-homology domain (Etoh and Fukuda, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: KIF13B and other members of the kinesin-3 family yield super processive motion when acting as dimers.
source: Interestingly, KIF13B and other members of the kinesin-3 family have been shown to yield super processive motion when acting as dimers (Soppina et al., 2014), helping to explain how even a relatively small increase in the recruitment of KIF13B onto axonal Rab10-positive organelle can trigger a rapid change in their transport directionality.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The activity of Rab10 is controlled by PI3K-Akt, a canonical BDNF/TrkB signalling pathway.
source: For example, the activity of Rab10 is known to be controlled by PI3K-Akt, a canonical BDNF/TrkB signalling pathway.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about Rab10 regulation.

claim: In adipocytes and muscle cells, Rab10 regulates the plasma membrane delivery of the glucose transporter GLUT4 in response to insulin.
source: In adipocytes and muscle cells, Rab10 is known to regulate the plasma membrane delivery of the glucose transporter GLUT4 in response to insulin, where activation of Akt leads to phosphorylation of the Rab GAP Akt substrate of 160 kDa (AS160).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about Rab10 function in adipocytes and muscle cells.

claim: Rab10 associated to GLUT4-containing endosomes is kept inactive by AS160 until Akt signalling releases the brake and promotes fusion with the plasma membrane.
source: Rab10 associated to GLUT4-containing endosomes is kept inactive by AS160 until Akt signalling releases the brake and promotes fusion with the plasma membrane (Sano et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Both anterograde and retrograde organelles have membrane-bound Rab10.
source: However, two key observations suggest that directionality of Rab10 organelles in the axon does not depend uniquely on Rab10 activity. First, both anterograde and retrograde organelles have membrane-bound Rab10 (Figure 5), which is generally accepted to be its GTP-bound active form.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The constitutively active Rab10Q68L mutant is transported predominantly in the retrograde direction in neurons depleted of BDNF.
source: Second, we observed that the constitutively active Rab10Q68L mutant is transported predominantly in the retrograde direction in neurons depleted of BDNF (see Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The GTP-bound conformation of Rab10 is necessary to drive its binding to the membrane of axonal organelles, but not sufficient to determine the direction of transport.
source: Altogether, these findings indicate that whilst the GTP-bound conformation of Rab10 is necessary to drive its binding to the membrane of axonal organelles, this alone is not sufficient to determine the direction of transport.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental observations about Rab10 activity and directionality.

claim: LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation of Rab10 in the switch II region affects its GTP/GDP cycle and its ability to bind effectors.
source: The LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation of Rab10 in the highly conserved switch II region has been proposed to affect its GTP/GDP cycle as well as its ability to bind effectors (Pfeffer et al., 1995; Xu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation of Rab10 regulates the interaction of Rab10 with JIP3 and JIP4.
source: Moreover, this phosphorylation site has been shown to regulate the interaction of Rab10 with JIP3 and JIP4 (Waschbüsch et al., 2020), which are adaptors for the plus-end-directed microtubule-dependent motor kinesin-1 (Cockburn et al., 2018; Isabet et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: JIP3 mediates the anterograde transport of TrkB in neurons and enhances BDNF signalling.
source: Interestingly, JIP3 has been shown to mediate the anterograde transport of TrkB in neurons and, by that mechanism, to enhance BDNF signalling (Huang et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: JIP3 and JIP4 association to Rab10 organelles is extremely low in hippocampal neurons and does not respond to BDNF stimulation.
source: However, preliminary experiments showed that JIP3 and JIP4 association to Rab10 organelles is extremely low in hippocampal neurons and does not respond to BDNF stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by preliminary experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: LRRK2-phosphorylated Rab10 recruits myosin Va.
source: LRRK2-phosphorylated Rab10 has been also found to recruit myosin Va (Dhekne et al., 2021), providing other candidates for regulation of axonal trafficking.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Positioning of Rab10-positive membranes determines their phosphorylation by LRRK2.
source: On the other hand, positioning of Rab10-positive membranes has been recently shown to determine their phosphorylation by LRRK2, suggesting that trafficking and composition of these organelles can be mutually regulated (Kluss et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10, KIF13B, and LRRK2 have been implicated in the formation of tubular endosomes.
source: However, it is worth mentioning that all three Rab10, KIF13B, and LRRK2 have been implicated in the formation of tubular endosomes (Bonet-Ponce et al., 2020; Etoh and Fukuda, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Vps35 is a component of the retromer complex that modulates LRRK2.
source: Among the most interesting candidates linking BDNF-signalling and LRRK2 activity is Vps35, a component of the retromer complex that has been shown to modulate LRRK2 (Mir et al., 2018) and is recruited by TrkB binding to SorLA (Rohe et al., 2013), a sortilin family member.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Vps35 is recruited by TrkB binding to SorLA.
source: Among the most interesting candidates linking BDNF-signalling and LRRK2 activity is Vps35, a component of the retromer complex that has been shown to modulate LRRK2 (Mir et al., 2018) and is recruited by TrkB binding to SorLA (Rohe et al., 2013), a sortilin family member.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of Akt compensates impairments of insulin-stimulated GLUT4 trafficking associated with LRRK2 deficiency.
source: On the other hand, activation of Akt has been shown to compensate impairments of the insulin-stimulated GLUT4 trafficking associated with LRRK2 deficiency (Funk et al., 2019), opening the possibility that other downstream kinases could regulate Rab10 by LRRK2-independent mechanisms.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Internalised axonal TrkB can either recycle back to the plasma membrane or undergo sorting to the retrograde axonal transport route.
source: Once internalised, axonal TrkB reaches early endosomes, from where it can either recycle back to the plasma membrane, thus fine-tuning the response of nerve terminals to BDNF (reviewed in Andreska et al., 2020) or undergo sorting to the retrograde axonal transport route, propagating neurotrophic signals to the soma (Deinhardt et al., 2006; Ha et al., 2008; Zhou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Delivery of Rab10 to axon terminals facilitates the sorting of TrkB to retrogradely transported organelles.
source: Given that Rab10 downregulation decreased retrograde transport of TrkB and stimulation with BDNF promoted anterograde transport of Rab10, we reasoned that delivery of Rab10 to axon terminals facilitated the sorting of TrkB to retrogradely transported organelles.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental observations about Rab10 and TrkB trafficking.

claim: The pool of TrkB receptors available for local recycling and axonal transport are spatially segregated in the early endosome membrane.
source: We demonstrated that Rab10DN expression increases the accumulation of internalised TrkB in early endosomes without significantly affecting recycling (Figure 7), suggesting that the pool of TrkB receptors available for local recycling and axonal transport are spatially segregated in the early endosome membrane, and thus indicating that functional Rab10 aids the exit of TrkB from early endosomes and its sorting to distinct axonal retrograde organelles.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Functional Rab10 aids the exit of TrkB from early endosomes and its sorting to distinct axonal retrograde organelles.
source: We demonstrated that Rab10DN expression increases the accumulation of internalised TrkB in early endosomes without significantly affecting recycling (Figure 7), suggesting that the pool of TrkB receptors available for local recycling and axonal transport are spatially segregated in the early endosome membrane, and thus indicating that functional Rab10 aids the exit of TrkB from early endosomes and its sorting to distinct axonal retrograde organelles.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Only p75NTR receptors are present in Rab10-containing anterograde organelles.
source: When overexpressed, Rab10 is found at detectable levels in retrograde signalling endosomes positive for TrkB or p75NTR (Figure 4). An interesting observation is that only p75 receptors are present in Rab10-containing anterograde organelles, which bears the question on the role of the anterograde delivery of p75NTR to distal axons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In sympathetic neurons, p75NTR is rapidly mobilised to the plasma membrane upon stimulation with NGF via activation of Arf6.
source: In sympathetic neurons, it has been shown that p75NTR is rapidly mobilised to the plasma membrane upon stimulation with NGF via activation of Arf6 (Hickman et al., 2018), a small GTPase that has been shown to share common organelles with Rab10 in Caenorhabditis elegans (Shi and Grant, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Arf6 shares common organelles with Rab10 in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: In sympathetic neurons, it has been shown that p75NTR is rapidly mobilised to the plasma membrane upon stimulation with NGF via activation of Arf6 (Hickman et al., 2018), a small GTPase that has been shown to share common organelles with Rab10 in Caenorhabditis elegans (Shi and Grant, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The absolute amount of retrograde TrkB associated to Rab10 organelles remains low at endogenous levels of Rab10.
source: At endogenous levels of Rab10, however, when we analysed triple co-localisation of internalised HCT and TrkB with endogenous Rab10, we found that the absolute amount of retrograde TrkB associated to Rab10 organelles remains low (Figure 3e), suggesting that this interaction is transient.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: In MDCK cells, Rab10 mediates transport from early endosomes to a polarised trafficking route.
source: This is in line with previous evidence showing that in MDCK cells, Rab10 mediates transport from early endosomes to a polarised trafficking route (Babbey et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In C. elegans, Rab10 is recruited to early endosomes where it downregulates Rab5, helping to select cargoes for delivery to recycling endosomes.
source: Moreover, in C. elegans, Rab10 is recruited to early endosomes where it downregulates Rab5, helping to select cargoes for delivery to recycling endosomes (Liu and Grant, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 is recruited to a TrkB-positive axonal organelle few seconds before it starts moving retrogradely.
source: Crucially, Rab10 is recruited to this TrkB-positive axonal organelle few seconds before it starts moving retrogradely, strengthening the validity of our working model (Figure 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 8b.

claim: Rab10 participates in the biogenesis of tubular endosomes in mammalian cells.
source: Rab10 has been shown to participate in the biogenesis of tubular endosomes in mammalian cells (Etoh and Fukuda, 2019) and regulates endosomal phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate in C. elegans, suggesting that this small GTPase modulates the membrane recruitment of factors altering membrane curvature and budding (Shi and Grant, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 regulates endosomal phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate in C. elegans.
source: Rab10 has been shown to participate in the biogenesis of tubular endosomes in mammalian cells (Etoh and Fukuda, 2019) and regulates endosomal phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate in C. elegans, suggesting that this small GTPase modulates the membrane recruitment of factors altering membrane curvature and budding (Shi and Grant, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10-positive tubular organelles move rapidly into proximal neurites in hippocampal neurons.
source: During our live-cell imaging experiments, we observed Rab10-positive tubular organelles moving rapidly into proximal neurites, confirming that these structures are also generated in hippocampal neurons (Figure 5—video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 5—video 3.

claim: Snapin is an adaptor for cytoplasmic dynein recruitment to TrkB-signalling endosomes.
source: In addition, it has been shown that snapin, an adaptor for cytoplasmic dynein recruitment to TrkB-signalling endosomes (Zhou et al., 2012), is also phosphorylated by LRRK2 (Yun et al., 2013), opening the possibility that Rab10 membranes constitute a specialised sorting domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Snapin is phosphorylated by LRRK2.
source: In addition, it has been shown that snapin, an adaptor for cytoplasmic dynein recruitment to TrkB-signalling endosomes (Zhou et al., 2012), is also phosphorylated by LRRK2 (Yun et al., 2013), opening the possibility that Rab10 membranes constitute a specialised sorting domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: KIF13B transports phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-biphosphate via its interactor centaurin-alpha.
source: Interestingly, one of the well-characterised roles of KIF13B in the brain is the transport of phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-biphosphate via its interactor centaurin-alpha (Hammonds-Odie et al., 1996), which is essential for axon specification (Horiguchi et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Centaurin-alpha is essential for axon specification.
source: Interestingly, one of the well-characterised roles of KIF13B in the brain is the transport of phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-biphosphate via its interactor centaurin-alpha (Hammonds-Odie et al., 1996), which is essential for axon specification (Horiguchi et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab10 regulates the amount of internalised TrkB that is sorted to retrograde signalling endosomes in response to the concentration of BDNF at axon terminals.
source: Our data suggests that Rab10 regulates the amount of internalised TrkB that is sorted to retrograde signalling endosomes in response to the concentration of BDNF at axon terminals.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing BDNF-dependent changes in Rab10 trafficking and TrkB sorting.

claim: BDNF is released post-synaptically as a function of neuronal activity.
source: Since BDNF is known to be released post-synaptically as a function of neuronal activity (Matsuda et al., 2009), retrograde neurotrophic signalling from the axon terminal is a substantial feedback mechanism regulating growth and survival, and therefore, ensuring that active circuits are preserved.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Rab10-positive membranes deliver crucial components of the sorting machinery on demand.
source: We propose that Rab10-positive membranes deliver crucial components of the sorting machinery on demand.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: At steady state, the anterograde and retrograde flow of Rab10 compartments is in equilibrium.
source: At steady state, the anterograde and retrograde flow of Rab10 compartments is in equilibrium (Figure 8; low BDNF).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Decrease in BDNF concentration makes retrograde transport of Rab10 carriers predominant.
source: Further decrease in BDNF concentration makes retrograde transport of Rab10 carriers predominant, as observed in live-cell imaging experiments performed in neurons treated with anti-BDNF blocking antibodies (Figure 4; no BDNF).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Adding BDNF reverts the directional bias of Rab10 carriers to anterograde.
source: In contrast, adding BDNF reverts the directional bias to anterograde (Figure 8; high BDNF), which allows the delivery of appropriate levels of the sorting machinery to nerve terminals, thus increasing the efficiency of TrkB retrograde transport.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and the model in Figure 8.

claim: Khc-73, the fly orthologue of KIF13B, regulates BMP sorting from early endosomes at the neuromuscular junction in Drosophila motor neurons.
source: An independent example of anterograde delivery of components for the sorting of retrograde signalling molecules has been hypothesised for the bone-morphogenetic protein (BMP) pathway in Drosophila motor neurons. In this work, Khc-73, the fly orthologue of KIF13B, has been shown to regulate BMP sorting from early endosomes at the neuromuscular junction (Liao et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The proposed mechanism of anterograde delivery of sorting machinery is evolutionary conserved in different neuronal types.
source: This suggests that the proposed mechanism is evolutionary conserved in different neuronal types, increasing its potential as a therapeutic target for pathologies in which neurotrophic signalling from distal axons is impaired.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison with the BMP pathway in Drosophila.

claim: Endophilins A1 and A3 regulate the trafficking of TrkB across early endosomes and mediate survival signalling.
source: Endophilins A1 and A3 have been shown to regulate the trafficking of TrkB across early endosomes and mediate survival signalling (Burk et al., 2017; Fu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Endophilin A1 and Rab10 are known LRRK2 substrates.
source: Interestingly, endophilin A1 as well as Rab10 are known LRRK2 substrates, opening the possibility of both being found on the same organelle (Matta et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: KIF13B is enriched in early endosomes.
source: Moreover, KIF13B has also been found to be enriched in early endosomes (Bentley et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Promoting the delivery of Rab10 organelles to nerve terminals may be explored as a novel therapeutic strategy for diseases with overloaded or dysfunctional endolysosomal systems.
source: In this light, promoting the delivery of Rab10 organelles to nerve terminals may be explored as an novel therapeutic strategy for diseases in which the endolysosomal system is overloaded or dysfunctional, such as Alzheimer's disease (Van Acker et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2018), or to increase the ability of axons to respond to trophic factors during regeneration.
evidence: This is a speculative therapeutic proposal based on the findings of the study.

claim: Hippocampal neurons were cultured from C57BL/6 mice of either sex at embryonic age 16-17 days.
source: Embryonic hippocampal neurons from C57BL/6 mice of either sex and embryonic age of 16–17 days were dissected adapting previously described protocols (Kaech and Banker, 2006).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Neurons were seeded at a density of 10,000-12,000 neurons per cm2.
source: 10,000–12,000 neurons per cm2 were then seeded on glass coverslips or microfluidic chambers, pre-coated with 1 mg/mL poly-L-lysine.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Microfluidic chambers provide cellular and fluidic compartmentalisation of axon terminals.
source: To study axonal TrkB dynamics, we cultured hippocampal neurons in microfluidic chambers, which allow the cellular and fluidic compartmentalisation of axon terminals.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods and their purpose.
